## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Catukkauddesa* is the fourth section of the summary matrix (*uddesa*) of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the fourth treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It presents an index or table of classifications of persons arranged in sets of four [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language and notes connections to *Sāvajjasutta* (AN 4.135), *Chavālātasutta* (AN 4.95), the *Puggalakathā* of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1), and its own detailed exposition chapter, the *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4) [SuttaCentral].
The text exhibits extensive textual reuse across the Pali Canon, with DharmaNexus detecting 531 matching passages across 24 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of its shared material aligns directly with the *Catukkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4, with 152 matches) and its companion expository section *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4, with 90 matches) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus aligns segments §26.1–26.5 of the text with identical fourfold classifications of persons found across several Majjhima Nikāya discourses, notably the *Ghoṭamukha Sutta* (MN 94), the *Kandaraka Sutta* (MN 51), and the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), as well as the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [DharmaNexus]. Additional textual matches are identified in AN 2, AN 5, AN 7, AN 9, AN 10, and commentarial works such as the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches meeting the scoring threshold of 10 [DharmaNexus].
